# ShouldIDive

> Free ocean-conditions map for the California and Baja California coast, built and run by one person. It combines satellite sea surface temperature, swell, wind, surface currents, chlorophyll, temperature breaks, marine protected areas, and detailed depth and kelp charts, plus a modeled visibility estimate whose measured error is published. No account and no ads.

Audiences: scuba divers and freedivers, spearfishers, offshore anglers, sailors and boaters, and ocean researchers.

## Pages

- [Live map](https://shouldidive.com/): the interactive app (JavaScript). Layers: Temp, Chl, Wind, Swell, Current, Vis. Overlays: MPAs, Bottom features, temperature Breaks.
- [Spots](https://shouldidive.com/spots/): one static page per saved spot (California and Baja) with today's water temperature, a swell and wind outlook, NOAA tides for California spots, kelp and depth chart facts, and protected areas. Rebuilt about hourly.
- [Diving](https://shouldidive.com/diving/): water temperature, swell and surge, visibility and how far to trust it, detailed charts.
- [Spearfishing](https://shouldidive.com/spearfishing/): MPA boundaries, kelp canopy, temperature breaks, kelp paddies, Mexico rules.
- [Fishing](https://shouldidive.com/fishing/): temperature breaks with GPS waypoints, chlorophyll edges, currents, banks and seamounts, Kelp Paddy Finder, Fleet Tracks.
- [Sailing](https://shouldidive.com/sailing/): wind out to seven days updated hourly, swell height, period, and direction, HF radar surface currents.
- [Science](https://shouldidive.com/science/): every data source, processing rules, and the visibility model's measured accuracy.
- [About](https://shouldidive.com/about/): what the site is, coverage, cost, and how to install it.

## Data sources

NASA JPL MUR sea surface temperature (via NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP, buoy-corrected in California); NASA OB.DAAC, NOAA DINEOF, and Copernicus Marine chlorophyll; NOAA HRRR, GFS, and ECMWF wind; NOAA WaveWatch III swell; IOOS HF radar surface currents; NOAA CO-OPS tides; Santa Barbara Coastal LTER Landsat kelp canopy; NOAA NCEI coastal elevation models and GMRT bathymetry; CDFW and CONANP protected-area boundaries; NOAA and US Coast Guard AIS for fleet tracks.

## Caveats

The visibility estimate is a model labelled Modeled. Scored against California dive reports it has not yet tracked day-to-day conditions; see the Science page for current numbers. Observed layers are never interpolated, so blank areas mean no data. Nothing on the site is an official marine forecast or a navigation chart.
